title: Anthropic Taps RetailBook to Market UK Retail Portion of Potential $100B IPO
summary:
The AI startup has arranged for the investing platform RetailBook to manage the sale of its shares to individual traders in Britain as part of its broader market debut. The partnership coincides with a formal filing for an initial public offering with the SEC, a move that allows the public to examine the company's financial statements for the first time.

Anthropic plans to allocate up to 20% of its potential $100B offering to retail investors, using Citigroup to coordinate distributions in markets including Canada, Japan and the UK. In the US, JPMorgan will lead the retail campaign, a role the bank previously held for SpaceX's $86.2B IPO. Despite the push for individual participation, reports indicate that retail investors in many Asian markets may find it difficult to obtain shares.

ANTHROPIC PICKED JPMORGAN $JPM TO LEAD SALES OF ITS IPO SHARES TO EVERYDAY INVESTORS

Anthropic has weighed setting aside about 15% to 20% of the IPO for individual investors, per Bloomberg. JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon is expected to take part in the bank's campaign.

JPMorgan ran the same role for SpaceX's $86.2B IPO, which drew more than $100B of demand from individual investors.

Citigroup will coordinate retail sales outside the US, including in the UK, Canada, Japan, and Australia.
